Fresh cooking + useful make-ahead

Prep

Prepare components that hold well. Cook proteins fresh, open tinned fish at serving, and assemble greens only when the bowl is served.

Protein, cooked fresh

Fresh salmon

Pat dry; season with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast or pan-sear until just opaque and flakes easily. Finish with lemon, dill, parsley, yuzu or spicy aioli. Cook fresh every time.

Haddock / bass

Season with olive oil, lemon, salt, pepper and dill or parsley. Bake until opaque and flakes easily. Use champagne-dill or Mediterranean vinaigrette.

Shrimp

Pat dry and sear quickly with olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper until opaque. Finish with lime, ginger, yuzu or chili.

Tofu

Press or pat very dry, cube, season and roast or sear until crisp. Add sauce after cooking so the edges stay crisp.

Chicken

Season and roast or pan-cook just before dinner; try lemon, sage or parsley. Only the slow-cooked mushroom chicken is an intentional reheat-well exception.

Home-ground turkey

Brown in a hot skillet with onion, garlic, cumin, paprika and Mexican mint / Cuban oregano used sparingly. Add tomato or chipotle as desired.

Tinned fish

Tuna, sardines, smoked sprats and canned smoked salmon are open-fresh: drain as needed and assemble at serving. They are not cooked proteins or PM scoop salads.

Slow-cooked mushroom chicken

The planned exception: chicken, mushrooms, onion, garlic and mushroom or chicken broth. Portion and refrigerate; reheat thoroughly, then serve over freshly dressed greens.

PM Reheats well.

Seasoned toasted nuts + seeds

For each 1 cup nuts or toastable seeds, toss with 1 tsp oil and ¼ tsp salt. Roast at 325°F / 165°C, checking and stirring often, until fragrant and lightly colored. Cool completely before storing.

Sturdy spices go on before roasting: paprika, chipotle, coriander, curry, cayenne and black pepper. Add delicate or powdery seasonings after roasting: za’atar, togarashi, nutritional yeast, dried dill and flaky salt. Add hemp after cooling.

Mediterranean

Walnuts + pumpkin seeds + sunflower seeds + za’atar.

Smoky

Cashews + sunflower seeds + paprika + chipotle.

Asian

Cashews or macadamia + sesame + togarashi.

Flaxmeal works in bread, dressings and scoops. Grind whole flax before using. Hydrate chia and basil seeds; they are not dry crunchy toppings.

Brazil nuts and selenium: A Brazil nut contains roughly 68–91 mcg selenium, while the US adult upper limit is 400 mcg per day. Selenium content varies. Use one occasionally as a shaved garnish, not a handful or daily bulk topping. NIH selenium guidance.
Useful · PM

Smoky corn

Skillet · best char

  1. Thaw or drain corn and pat very dry.
  2. Heat a wide skillet until hot. Toss 2 cups corn with 1 tsp oil, ½ tsp smoked paprika, ¼ tsp cumin, chipotle and salt.
  3. Add in one layer; leave 2–3 minutes, stir, then cook 4–5 minutes more.
  4. Finish off heat with lime and chopped parsley or scallion; add feta when slightly cool.

Oven · hands-off

Heat oven and sheet pan to 450°F / 230°C. Toss dry corn with oil and seasoning, spread on the hot pan and roast 15–20 minutes, stirring once. Do not crowd the pan.

Useful · PM

Flourless buckwheat bread

Ingredients

2 cups raw buckwheat groats
¾–1 cup water
2 Tbsp flaxmeal
1 Tbsp chia
1 tsp salt
1 tsp gluten-free baking powder
Optional pumpkin seeds, hemp or walnuts

Method

  1. Soak groats 4–6 hours. Drain, rinse and blend with ¾ cup fresh water.
  2. Stir in flaxmeal, chia, salt, baking powder and optional seeds. Rest 15 minutes.
  3. Bake in a lined loaf pan at 350°F / 175°C for 55–65 minutes.
  4. Cool completely. Refrigerate or freeze, then toast; Pacha croutons can also be prepared ahead.
Useful · PM

Grains + bowl bases

Cook quinoa or wild rice ahead, cool promptly and refrigerate. Warm a portion for the bowl, then add to fresh greens. Corn grits can also make a warm base; use a gluten-free labeled product when strict avoidance matters. Roasted broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts and mushrooms hold well; keep greens separate until serving.
